messages:
sasha: CI red on PR #4123 — nightly `transformer_smoke` failed on a canary H100 node with `invalid device function` during kernel launch. job: https://ci.internal/redwood/abcd1234 :eyes:
ci-bot: build 4123-566 failed (h100-warmup). test: transformer_smoke. exit 1. logs archived: https://ci.internal/artifacts/abcd1234/logs.tar.gz
devin: can you paste the tail of the test run and the cuda error? quick checks: `kubectl logs -n ci job/h100-warmup-566` and `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- dmesg | tail -n 50`
sasha: here's the relevant snippet:
```
[2025-04-15 03:12:09] ERROR: cuBLAS launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE_FUNCTION
  at /src/runtime/kernel.cu:line 214
  kernel: fused_attention_forward_kernel
  ptidx: 0
```
anand: invalid device function usually means PTX/kernel not compatible with the driver or compiled for a newer SM. what is the container CUDA runtime version vs host driver? `nvidia-smi` from the node will tell us. canary nodes recently got a driver bump? :thinking:
leo: iirc we started a gradual driver rollout yesterday. canary pool moved from 535.xx -> 536.2x. that could explain mismatch if container bundles cubin for different sm.
sasha: ok i'll fetch `nvidia-smi` from the failing node and also rerun the job on non-canary to see if it repros. giving ops the node name: `ci-h100-canary-7`
ops: confirmed driver on ci-h100-canary-7: 536.21.03, kernel module built by our packaging. non-canary pool still at 535.45. trying to find rollout window in the driver deploy logs.
rachel: another quick workaround is to force the test image to use `--gpu-arch=sm_80` or fallback to PTX JIT if possible, but that's a code change. prefer infra fix first.
sasha: queued a rerun on a non-canary node and also triggered a rerun on the same canary node (keeping same commit). rerun ids: 4123-567 (non-canary), 4123-568 (canary).
ci-bot: rerun 4123-567 started on pool h100-nonc, rerun 4123-568 queued on pool h100-canary.
devin: if non-canary passes and canary fails consistently, that's strong signal for driver mismatch. can we bisect when the driver rollout started? which jobs started failing after that time?
sasha: results: 4123-567 passed, 4123-568 failed again with same `invalid device function`. logs: https://ci.internal/artifacts/abcd1234/rerun-568/logs.tar.gz
anand: yep that's consistent. ops, can you confirm which wave included that node? we need a bisect window (approx time when 536.xx started).
ops: driver rollout began 2025-04-14 22:10 UTC, wave 1 included canary-4..8. previous driver was 535.45. rollout cause: vendor security patch. i'll pull the map of jobs that transitioned.
leo: offer: i can repro locally if ops provisions one node with 535.45 and one with 536.21.03 and we run the test binary. if that's heavy, we can try to run the failing kernel with `cuobjdump` to inspect PTX vs CUBIN.
sasha: that would help. if we can repro, we can either pin the job to older pool or add a quick guard in the test harness to skip on mismatched driver for now.
anand: long-term we should publish supported driver matrix per image. short-term, ops can revert that single canary node to 535 to unblock nightly while we triage.
ops: reverting single node to previous driver now for canary-7. will report back when node is back up (~10m).
sasha: thanks — i'll watch CI. assigning follow-up to leo to run local repro and to anand to coordinate image compatibility check. :thumbsup:
leo: on it, starting local repro now. will paste steps and short repro if found.
sasha: update: after revert, rerun 4123-569 on canary-7 passed. looks like driver is culprit. filing a short incident note and scheduling a controlled rollout pause. :relieved:
